races.title: State Senate, District 22
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Susan Rubio
cands.bio: Democratic state senator for District 22 (eastern Los Angeles County) since December 2018. Former public school teacher for 17 years, Baldwin Park city clerk from 2005, and Baldwin Park City Council member from 2009. Chairs the Senate Insurance Committee.

controversies.text: A former Baldwin Park city attorney's plea agreement, unsealed December 2024, alleges an unnamed official sought $30,000 in cash for a 2018 state campaign. The LA Times reported only Rubio fits the description. She isn't named or charged and denies taking bribes. Her spokesman says the FBI told her she isn't a target.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Teachers Association, and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Rubio on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and the 2018 survey did not touch these topics. We found no statements from her on development or data centers. The Ballotpedia list of bills she sponsored was empty in the page we read. We could not confirm the details of the 2018 cannabis corruption investigation beyond a secondhand summary, and we found no official finding about her. We did not find a source on her time in Texas beyond a short mention of the family's early years.

local.label: Roots 80: Born in Ciudad Juárez, she came to Los Angeles with her family in 1977 as a young child, and she has worked in Baldwin Park and the state Senate since.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2018 and chair of the Senate Insurance Committee. Before that, Baldwin Park city clerk (2005), city council member (2009–2018), a 17-year teacher in Monrovia Unified, and a bookkeeper handling payroll and taxes for a small business.
qual.why: Several terms of state legislative service, plus local elected office and a bookkeeping background involving payroll and taxes, fit the job of writing law and the budget. Committee chairmanship was not counted.

cands.name: Mike Netter
cands.bio: Mike Netter is a business owner and Republican who ran for California State Senate District 22 in 2026. He earned a bachelor's degree from San Diego State University in 1979. He says he began in sales and built a business. He has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, and Reform California, are listed among his endorsements on Ballotpedia.

In his Ballotpedia survey he lists endorsements from the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC, the Los Angeles County Taxpayers Association, Rep. Tom McClintock, Rep. Kevin Kiley, former Senate Majority Leader Gloria Romero, Sen. Shannon Grove and Assemblyman Carl DeMaio. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Mike Netter was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found nothing naming his business or describing its size or industry, so his business background rests on his own account. His claim that he led the effort to put the Newsom recall on the ballot isn't backed by any source we read. He has held no public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, guns, abortion or schools. We found no documented controversies about him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Business owner who says he started in sales, built a business and rose to executive level in his industry; he holds a 1979 bachelor's degree from San Diego State University and has held no elected office.
qual.why: Business ownership and management places him in the middle band; he has no legislative, policy or budget record, and his business history is self-described and not independently verified.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says Gov. Newsom refuses to let police turn convicted criminals who are in the country illegally over for deportation, a position favoring state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

back-police-order.evidence: His Ballotpedia survey says Gov. Newsom fought against efforts to increase penalties for smash-and-grab theft and that convicted criminals are being released; he campaigns on safer neighborhoods and holding criminals accountable.
